data.title: DSI to forward Forex-3D scam dossier to prosecutors
data.description: The Department of Special Investigation (DSI) is expected to forward its completed case file in the high-profile Forex-3D investment fraud investigation to public prosecutors this week.

data.title: Farmers oppose seed changes
data.description: Farmer groups and their civil society allies will gather at the Agriculture Ministry on Wednesday to oppose draft legal changes that would align Thailand with an international convention granting plant breeders stronger intellectual property rights over new seed varieties.

data.title: Ja Thawee dies at age 92
data.description: Thawee Buranakhet, better known as Ja Thawee, a National Artist renowned for his sculpture and bronze casting, has died at the age of 92.

data.title: Free MRT rides for bike, e-scooter users
data.description: Passengers travelling with bicycles or foldable electric scooters will be able to use the MRT network for free today as part of World Car Free Day 2026.

data.title: Seniors urged to use traditional Chinese medicine  to slow cognitive decline
data.description: Older people are being encouraged to adopt four daily practices based on traditional Chinese medicine to help maintain brain health and slow cognitive decline.

data.title: Air hostess heroin case advances
data.description: The Office of the Attorney-General (OAG) has ordered the indictment of four suspects allegedly linked to a transnational drug trafficking network involving Thai Airways flight attendant Meena Kondo in a heroin smuggling case.

data.title: Amnesty panel sets out process
data.description: A new committee tasked with promoting social peace will push ahead with an amnesty process aimed at ending political conflicts that have persisted for more than two decades, said Deputy Prime Minister Pakorn Nilprapunt.

data.title: Democrats petition for audit of TH-AI Passport
data.description: The Democrat Party on Monday petitioned the Auditor-General to investigate the 1.621-billion-baht TH-AI Passport project, raising seven concerns over procurement, payment criteria, AI performance, project targets and data governance.

data.title: Navy commander defends frigate bid
data.description: Navy Commander‑in‑Chief Adm Pairoj Fuangchan said on Monday that the bidding process for a new naval frigate was transparent and that the navy has no concerns about scrutiny of its procurement process.

data.title: MRT Blue Line back to normal
data.description: Normal MRT Blue Line services resumed Monday morning after an electrical fault near Tao Poon station damaged power and signalling equipment and disrupted services on Sunday.

data.title: Govt racing to conclude US tariff negotiations
data.description: Thailand is seeking to conclude trade negotiations with the United States before Washington announces the results of investigations into Thai trade practices that could lead to additional tariffs, Deputy Prime Minister and Commerce Minister Suphajee Suthumpun said.

data.title: PM eyes stronger Japan ties
data.description: Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul on Monday urged Thailand and Japan to move from producing goods for one another to producing them together, saying closer supply-chain ties would help sustain Japanese investment as the automotive industry shifts towards electric vehicles.

data.title: City Hall working on new master drainage plan for Bangkok
data.description: Bangkok's City Hall has partnered with a Japanese government agency in designing a long-term urban drainage master plan to prepare the capital for heavier rainfall, with a target of coping with 100 millimetres of rain per hour.

data.title: Free MRT rides for cyclists, e-scooter users on World Car Free Day, Tuesday
data.description: Passengers bringing bicycles or foldable electric scooters onto the MRT rail network on Tuesday will travel for free, because it's World Car Free Day 2026.

data.title: Woman buys gold ring on popular app, receives fake instead
data.description: NAKHON RATCHASIMA - A woman who was conned into buying a fake gold ring through a popular e-commerce platform recounted her experience on Monday as a warning to other online shoppers.

data.title: Ministry demands apology over Cambodian claim to Thai historical photograph
data.description: The Thai Ministry of Culture has sent a letter demanding an apology from Miss Universe Cambodia over its misuse of a historical Thai photograph, believing it was done intentionally to cause misunderstanding about the picture's origin.

data.title: Rising water levels warning for Chao Phraya Basin provinces
data.description: The Royal Irrigation Department issued a warning on Monday for residents of 11 provinces in the Chao Phraya River Basin, including Bangkok - prepare for rising water levels as heavy rain in the north increases the river's flow.

data.title: Skytrain delays due to problem at Asok station
data.description: Skytrain services were suffering delays on the Sukhumvit Line because of a problem at Asok station, the BTS operator said on Monday.

data.title: Call centre gangs turn to new tricks
data.description: Two university students were rescued from call-centre gangs earlier this month after scammers posing as officials manipulated them into transferring large sums of money and cutting themselves off from their families.

data.title: Senate lines up B112m  for Koh Kut military road
data.description: The Senate has coordinated with agencies to secure a 112 million baht budget for a 5km road on Koh Kut in Trat, with the project expected to be completed in 2028.

data.title: Over B161bn spent under co-payment scheme: govt
data.description: Spending under the government's Thais Help Thais Plus 60/40 co-payment scheme has surpassed 161 billion baht, and the Finance Ministry will ask the cabinet tomorrow to consider extending the programme.

data.title: EC refers 36 to Supreme Court over poll collusion
data.description: The Election Commission (EC) will petition the Supreme Court and pursue criminal charges against 36 people over alleged collusion in the Senate election, while dismissing complaints against 135 others.

data.title: Day of reckoning for rival tech schools
data.description: Rajamangala University of Technology Tawan-Ok's Uthenthawai Campus and the Pathumwan Institute of Technology (PIT), two of Bangkok's oldest technical institutions, were ordered on Sept 9 to suspend on-site teaching for at least three months.

data.title: Phuket steps up Chabad Patong probe
data.description: Phuket authorities are investigating products sold at Chabad Patong, including labelling, health standards and import legality, as part of a seven-day probe ordered by governor Chotenarin Kerdsom.

data.title: Media explores AI opportunities, risks
data.description: The Thai Journalists Association (TJA) and the Lao Journalists Association (LJA) have reaffirmed their partnership, highlighting both the opportunities and risks posed by artificial intelligence (AI) in regional reporting.

data.title: Townsend hit by pitch roller
data.description: The Football Association of Thailand has spoken out after Andros Townsend, the 35-year-old former England international forward of PT Prachuap FC, was struck by a pitch roller while warming up with his teammates during half-time in their match against Pattani FC.

data.title: US tariff deal  'taking shape'
data.description: Thailand has secured its desired tariff rate it sought from the United States but one additional condition raised by Washington remains to be finalised, Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul said on Sunday.

data.title: PM vows no special treatment
data.description: Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul has vowed not to protect anyone suspected of fraud in local government recruitment exams, saying he is awaiting further details before deciding whether further action is needed.

data.title: Most 'unfazed' by Senate case: poll
data.description: More than half of respondents to a Nida Poll survey are not worried that the Election Commission's decision to prosecute 77 people, including 26 sitting senators, over alleged collusion in the 2024 Senate election will cause political unrest.

data.title: Repair crews battle to reopen Blue Line for Monday rush hours
data.description: Trains running on the Blue Line of Bangkok's fire-damaged Mass Rapid Transit system would resume full services on Monday morning if overnight repairs were complete and guaranteed safe, Deputy Transport Minister Phattrapong Phattraprasit said on Sunday.
